data.description: Heavy coal and chrome haulage causes severe road deterioration, particularly on secondary routes linking mines to national corridors. Mpumalanga's N4, N11, and N17 carry extreme volumes â€” in one 12-hour period, 34,198 tonnes of freight were recorded on the N4 between Nelspruit and Komatipoort. Most roads in Limpopo's Waterberg District (8,500km) are unpaved (only 30% paved). Gravel roads in Burgersfort-Steelpoort area accelerate tyre wear and increase maintenance costs.
data.monitoring_source: SA Freight Data Banks (Mpumalanga, Limpopo, KZN)

data.description: SA's weighbridge network targets major freight corridors. On the N4, weighbridges are managed by TRAC under SANRAL contract with Mpumalanga DPWRT enforcement. The N11 and N17 are monitored from the Ermelo Traffic Control Centre. Approximately 20% of weighed vehicles are found overloaded nationally. March 2026 Tshwane Metro operation: 31 of 88 inspected trucks failed overload compliance. Penalties include fines and removal from road. RTMS certification is a key differentiator showing voluntary compliance above legal minimum.
data.monitoring_source: Mpumalanga Freight Data Bank; Limpopo DTCS Weighbridge Registry

data.description: Diesel is the largest single operating cost, representing 35â€“55% of daily operating cost per vehicle. March 2026 diesel shock: R10.34/litre price increase (56%). South Africa's diesel price is set monthly by the Department of Energy using an import parity pricing (Basic Fuel Price) mechanism linked to Brent crude and Rand/USD exchange rate. SA operators pay for diesel upfront on 60â€“90-day invoice cycles, creating cash flow exposure. Fuel hedge mechanisms are rare for small/mid-size operators.
data.monitoring_source: Department of Energy / Fuels Industry Association of South Africa monthly price announcements

data.description: South Africa has a structural shortage of qualified heavy vehicle drivers (Code EC and EC1 licences). Driver wages are governed by the NBCRFLI sectoral determination. Wage disputes and strikes at NBCRFLI level can cause industry-wide disruption. High unemployment nationally (32.7%) coexists with a shortage of licensed, experienced long-haul drivers. Driver fatigue regulation (NRTA hours-of-service rules) limits productivity on long routes. Driver poaching between operators is common, increasing wage pressure.
data.monitoring_source: NBCRFLI (National Bargaining Council for the Road Freight and Logistics Industry); Road Freight Association (RFA)

data.description: Copper cable theft on the Transnet coal line declined from 180km (2024) to 59km (2025), but road freight theft remains a risk. High-value commodity trucks (coal, chrome) are targets for armed robbery and product theft, particularly on Mpumalanga N4 and N17 routes at night.
data.monitoring_source: SAPS crime statistics; Road Freight Association security advisories

data.risk_category: Transnet Rail Disruptions as Demand Amplifier
data.description: When Transnet Freight Rail suffers line outages, derailments, or capacity constraints, bulk mineral volumes shift to road â€” creating surge demand but also route congestion and road damage acceleration. Monitor TFR corridor performance monthly. Rail liberalisation introducing private operators from 2025â€“2026 may stabilise but initially disrupt road/rail split.
data.monitoring_source: Transnet Freight Rail Corridor Updates; Rail Journal
